title: Follow the Path in Nested Data
content:
What problem does this solve?
Real records combine familiar pieces: lists and dictionaries together. A party is a list of member dictionaries; a dispatch can hold a list under a key. You select one step at a time: party[0] picks a record from the list; party[0]["health"] reads a value from that dictionary. A loop can visit each smaller record in a larger model. enumerate(party, start=1) provides both a display number and each member record.

Previously in your program
You built dictionaries and lists, looped over each, and returned structured results. Now you read and update values one step into nested structures and assemble results from them.

Basic syntax
  party = [{"name": "Mira", "health": 8}, {"name": "Rook", "health": 10}]
  first = party[0]
  hp = party[0]["health"]
  dispatch = {"supplies": ["rope", "torch"]}
  dispatch["supplies"].append("map")
  for index, member in enumerate(party, start=1):
      print(index, member["name"])
concepts: party[0] selects a dictionary from a list
party[0]["health"] reads a value from that dictionary
dispatch["supplies"] selects a list stored inside a dictionary
A loop can visit each smaller record in a larger model
enumerate(party, start=1) provides both a display number and the member record
Big models are built from smaller structures

examples.title: Two steps along the path
examples.explanation: Select the first member dictionary, then its health, and update it.

examples.title: Enumerate names
examples.explanation: enumerate supplies both a display number and the record.

common_mistakes: Asking dispatch["name"] when the name lives inside a nested party record
Forgetting to index the party list before reading a member key
Appending to a new list rather than the one stored under a key
Trying to traverse arbitrary depths instead of one or two clear steps

exercises.title: Follow the path
hints: party[0] selects the first member dictionary.
Now read the same member's health again.

exercises.title: Look inside the party
exercises.prompt: Fix the access path so the program prints the first member's name.
hints: The outer dictionary has keys like destination and party.
party holds a list with one member dictionary at index 0.
Index the party list, then read the name key from that member.

tests.message: Read the name from the first party record: dispatch["party"][0]["name"], not a top-level "name".

exercises.title: Append to the inner list
exercises.prompt: Complete the expression so append affects the list stored in the dictionary.
hints: dispatch stores a list under the supplies key.
Index the dictionary by that key first.

tests.message: Append to the list stored at the supplies key so the printed list shows both items.

exercises.title: Total party health
exercises.prompt: Write total_party_health(party) that loops over a list of member dictionaries, adds each member's "health", and returns the total.
hints: Loop over each member dictionary and add member["health"].

tests.message: Use a for loop inside total_party_health to visit each member.
A single member's health becomes the total.
Two members with 8 and 10 should total 18.

exercises.title: Numbered roster
exercises.prompt: Write numbered_roster(party) using enumerate(party, start=1). Return one list of strings in the form: '1. Mira — 8 HP'.
hints: enumerate(party, start=1) provides both the number and the member record.
Use member["name"] and member["health"] inside the loop.
Append each formatted line to a list and return it.

tests.name: enumerate
tests.message: Call enumerate(...) inside numbered_roster to get both the display number and the member record.
An empty party should return an empty list.
One member should produce one correctly numbered line starting at 1.
Three members should produce three ordered lines numbered 1–3.
Do not hardcode names or counts — format the provided records.
